newsitem.title: USA: Shareholders sue Argentina's BAESA, PepsiCo.
newsitem.headline: Shareholders sue Argentina's BAESA, PepsiCo.

text.p: Shareholders of Buenos Aires Embotelladora SA (BAESA), PepsiCo's biggest South American bottler, filed a class-action suit in Manhattan federal court on Monday against both companies alleging they hid the bottler's problems.

Both companies made "materially false and misleading" statements that painted a "promising and upbeat picture of BAESA," highlighting its expansion possibilities and blaming the initial signs of trouble on the Argentine economy, the suit said.
Because the companies did not disclose BAESA's operational and management problems, the suit said, "BAESA securities traded at artificially inflated prices".

On July 2, BAESA announced that its losses to be "a multiple of" previous quarterly losses, the suit said. The company also announced $92.9 million in write-offs, including $30.1 million for "the physical loss of bottles, coolers and other tools of the trade", the complaint said.
Several individuals filed the suit on behalf of anyone who bought shares and bonds of BAESA between November 16, 1995, and July 2, 1996.
James Parker, an Anaheim, California, lawyer for the plantiffs, said that the stock suffered a loss of about $17 per share throughout the period -- from approximately $23 down to $5 3/4.
However, he said, under new rules that measure damages by the stock price 90 days before the company's full disclosure, they could only expect to recover about $7 per share.
PepsiCo did not return a request for comment.
PepsiCo announced last week that it would take a $525 million restructuring charge because of troubles in its Latin American bottling.
